We notice who sounds tired. We remember the date that carries weight. A familiar place gets more comfortable before anyone asks. rows.tension: The cost appears when care becomes the safest way to hide a need. We track everyone else's moods, keep things comfortable, and say nothing about what would help us. Then an ordinary change can feel like rejection. We defend an old arrangement because it once kept someone safe. We hold close to a role that no longer fits because being needed has become part of who we are. The support is real, but resentment builds when nobody notices what was never said.
